recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Collapse per-row statements inside loops into one set-based statement.

architectural_decisions.decision: Collapsed the cursor loop (fee lookup, account debit, TARIFA insert, audit log per row) into a single statement with data-modifying CTEs (calculadas -> atualizadas/tarifas_inseridas/log_por_transacao/log_lote).
architectural_decisions.rationale: All logic is pure relational computation; set-based SQL preserves semantics while removing four round-trips per transaction.

architectural_decisions.decision: The UPDATE debits each account once using SUM(taxa) grouped by conta_origem_id instead of one UPDATE per transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: A plain UPDATE ... FROM with multiple matching rows per account would apply only one (nondeterministic) fee; aggregating reproduces the cumulative effect of the original sequential loop.

architectural_decisions.decision: No commit/rollback in the function; everything runs on the caller's connection/transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The original procedure ran inside the caller's transaction; atomicity of the whole batch is preserved.

architectural_decisions.decision: LEFT JOIN LATERAL with WHERE percentual IS NOT NULL reproduces the original CONTINUE when no vigent fee row exists.
architectural_decisions.rationale: SELECT INTO leaves NULLs when no row is found, and the original skips those transactions.

architectural_decisions.decision: Introduced LoteTaxasError; the original had no RAISE, so it is only raised on unexpected execution failure.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Rule 5 requires typed exceptions; normal-path behaviour (no exceptions raised) is unchanged.

warnings: The original CASE kept TRANSFERENCIA fees unchanged and applied 1.10/0.90 multipliers; the multiplier is now computed in SQL with identical semantics.

The original loop debited accounts sequentially; the set-based version debits each account once with the summed fees. Net saldo result is identical, but any row-level triggers on contas fire once per account instead of once per transaction.
The final SELECT returns summary counts for logging only; the procedure still returns nothing to the caller, preserving the original contract.
DATE(data_transacao) is not sargable; consider indexing an expression or a generated date column if performance becomes an issue (same behaviour as legacy).
